title: Creating a Low-Cost RFID System with Business Central and Power Automate
summary: Building a low-cost RFID scan-in and scan-out system using an ESP32 microcontroller, PN532 RFID reader, Power Automate, and Business Central tables. The system captures location-based scans for resource tracking, automatically handles edge cases like forgotten scan-outs, and stores results in two related tables for monitoring.
key_points: The hardware is an ESP32 DEVKIT V1 with a PN532 RFID reader on the I2C bus, configured through a web portal with Wi-Fi, location and the Power Automate endpoint
Power Automate sits in the middle so the device avoids OAuth; its HTTP trigger parses the JSON array and sends each scan to a Business Central API page
The ARD_Scans table stores raw scans, and its OnInsert trigger creates or closes records in the ARD_ScanTracker table
If a tag scans in at a new location while still open somewhere else, the earlier record gets a scan-out time and is flagged as assumed for review
The device buffers up to 50 timestamped scans locally in case Wi-Fi is down

quotes.text: From this design the possibilities really open up. We can associate the RFID Tags with resources and track labor, or machine use time.
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates extensibility potential for using the scan system beyond basic tracking, such as labor analytics and equipment utilization measurement
